reasons.vendor: rule #59 reason: ram 6144 vs EVE 3072 - live-observed 2026-07-21 (config-lifecycle sweep round 7): 3 instances hung at 100% of a 4096MB cap under memory pressure; 6144 gives margin (see comment below). Do not lower.
reasons.min_ram_mb:
min_ram_mb=4096 matches Cisco's own documented CSR1000v IOS-XE 17.3 minimum (1/2/4
vCPU configs all list 4GB RAM as the floor - Cisco CSR1000v release notes). But
default_ram_mb was set equal to that floor, giving the launched VM zero headroom
above the bare minimum - live-observed 2026-07-21 (config-lifecycle sweep, round 7):
3 different csr1000vng-universalk9 instances all climbed to 100% of the 4096MB cap
and sat there for 3+ minutes before host-guard's hang-watchdog killed them for 0%
CPU (a real hang under memory pressure, not a slow-but-progressing boot - the
watchdog only fires on zero forward progress). 3 OTHER csr1000v/csr1000vng
instances in the same catalog HAD already passed earlier under lighter host load -
consistent with a device running exactly at its bare floor tipping over under real
hypervisor overhead + host contention, not a deterministic per-image failure.
default_ram_mb raised to 6144 (1.5x the floor) for real working margin, matching
this file's own pattern elsewhere (default set meaningfully above min, e.g.
barracuda/pfsense) - min_ram_mb stays at Cisco's documented 4096 floor, unchanged.
